section:
## 2. Two geometries under one boundary

Let the boundary contain applicable authorisations, competition duties, ethical
requirements and documentation obligations. Let a workflow specify how
activities proceed inside that boundary.

A **tunnel** is a workflow in which activities and approvals are substantially
pre-ordered. It can support predictability, repeatability and a clear decision
trail. It can also create queues, repeated hand-offs and late discovery of
requirement problems.

A **field** is a workflow in which an authorised team may parallelise, revisit
or select activities while the same boundary remains in force. It can support
earlier learning and different sequencing. It can also require additional
discovery work and create greater discretion if market-access controls are
weakened.

In Polish public procurement, both counterfactuals must comply with PZP. Mandatory submission
and standstill periods are fixed and identical in the two ProcuraCost
alternatives. Comparing a lawful procedure with an unlawful direct award would
not identify the effect of workflow design.
